utterances.text: And the fourth bus, number 4.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Did you, Mrs. Dosen, see any differences between those four buses that you saw from your position in numbers -- letter C?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes. The difference was in that three of the buses were white civilian city buses, and the fourth one, or rather the third one, to be precise, was a military bus, olive-drab. And around the bus there were four soldiers --

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Yeah, we can take that later on. Now just talking about the buses themselves. You just mentioned here that there was a military bus. Which one of the four was that, and will you please circle, make a circle around that number of that bus that was a military bus?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: I interrupted you a bit before. And you were on your way to tell us what -- there were differences between these buses. You mention it was a military bus and there was also, as I understood you right, another difference as well. And what was that then, please?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: The difference was that there were soldiers with automatic rifles or machine-guns standing around that military bus and that was where they took my husband. His stretcher was lowered beside that military bus. And that is why I can describe that particular bus best of all.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: You say there were soldiers with automatic rifles. How many soldiers were -- do you remember that? How many soldiers were by that specific bus, the military bus, bus number 3?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I remember precisely that there were four soldiers standing outside the bus, and there were two soldiers on the bus. Next to the driver's seat.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And once again, what kind of soldiers were the four and the two soldiers? Four around and the two inside the bus.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: All six of them were reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. So -- what happened with your husband? He was on stretchers. What happened with him? Can you tell us that, please?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: When we reached that bus they wanted to put Martin on the bus, but they just couldn't because the stretcher was too wide for the door. So they couldn't put him on the bus and he was unable to move himself or indeed to sit down, so they just lowered the stretcher on the ground. Tanja and I stood right there beside the stretcher, and Martin was outside the bus sitting on the ground on top of the stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. Can you also mark that on that photograph? You said that he was sitting on the ground on the stretchers. Can you please mark that on the photograph? And then we are on the letter F now. So please mark an F where Martin was sitting on the stretchers.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: The bus was here, so this would be it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Where were you and Tanja then when Martin was at the location F?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: We were standing next to him and beside the stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, you told us before that names were called up from a list that we have heard about. The people that were called out from that list, where were they heading to? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes. The people whose names I had heard called out, the four of them ended up on this military bus, number 3. But there two other men whose names I heard being called out who ended up in the bus marked as number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the names of that four people -- persons that ended up in the military bus, please?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Tadija Dosen, Ivan Dosen, the young Vulic, and Martin Jakubovski Dosen.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Did you see who instructed them on to this bus, the third bus?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: I don't know who it was that told them to get on that third bus, but by the time we arrived with the stretcher they were already on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: When you saw that, Mrs. Dosen, when they were already on the bus, how did the bus look inside? Could you have a possibility to make -- to see that, how the bus was constructed, so to say, inside the bus itself?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And what did you see?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: I saw that there were rows with two seats together on the bus, but they weren't sitting in pairs. There was one man per seat. Not two people together, but one behind the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. Was there any -- anything happened when you were standing there outside this third bus and you saw four people that you have mentioned by name sitting inside the bus, did anything happened to any of these people that were already in the bus when you were standing outside the bus? Either anything happened to the outside or inside the bus?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes. What happened was that Martin's youngest brother, Ivan Dosen, was taken off the bus suddenly by two soldiers. He was forced to walk toward the fence, which you can see in the photograph. They told him to raise his arms, and one of the men cocked his machine-gun and pointed it at him. At this point in time, the elder brother, Tadija, rose inside the bus, to see where his brother was being taken. And I was asked, "Ljubica, for God's sake, what's happening, where are they taking Bratsvo [phoen] to?" And I said, "I have no idea. You see there is probably something going on there." And he started saying things like, something's wrong, please take my child away from here, you see that there are no women or children here. This can't be a good thing. Meanwhile, while this was happening, on the other side of the fence with Ivan, women and children were being brought over from the direction marked as C. Ruzica Markobasic, Martin's sister --

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, we will stop here and just concentrate on the event with brother Ivan Dosen, and then after that we will move on, later on to the next incident. Can you please take the photograph again and mark on the photograph with the letter G where Ivan Dosen, you said that he was taken off the bus and there was a fence.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: So what are you doing now, Mrs. Dosen? Explain that for us. What does that show, that letter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's what you just asked her to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: I know. I want her to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've asked her to do it, she's marked it, you don't need anything more.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: What happened exactly at that point, Mrs. Dosen, when -- with brother Ivan Dosen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: He was taken to that fence and told to raise his arms. He was frisked and they told him that he was an Ustasha butcher and that he must have a knife on him somewhere. They grabbed him by his jacket from the back, and then he told him, "I don't have a knife on me," and the other man told him, "Go on then, you Ustasha, get on the bus," so he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And you said earlier here, Mrs. Dosen, there was an -- meanwhile there was another incident happening. Can you tell us about what happened then? You mentioned a female name, if I remember it right now.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Ruzica Markobasic, she's Martin's cousin. She lived with Davor Markobasic. They were yelling at him saying that he was an Ustasha, so she too was now brought over and told to go to the fence. Her fur coat was stripped from her, and they looked inside her bag for a necklace that had allegedly been made by her children by cutting -- made by her husband by cutting off children's fingers in order to make a necklace for her. This was an absurd notion, if you ask me. She was five months pregnant at this time, so you can imagine how scared and fearful she was. They told her that she was an Ustasha whore and then she told them that she didn't have anything like that, so then she was shoved aside too and ordered to go to that military bus. She was the only woman on that bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. Can you please mark with an H where she was put against the fence?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And you are referring -- thank you, Mrs. Dosen. You are referring to that "they" did took her to the bus. Who are "they"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Two soldiers who searched her near that fence. They led her to the bus and told her to get on the bus. Meanwhile, another soldier came back from the bus, grabbed me by the hand, and put something into my hand. I pressed my fist, because I thought that maybe it was a message that she was sending me. When I opened my fist, I realised that there were 2.000 dinars inside my fist. I stopped him and said, "Listen, young man, I have no use for this." And his answer was, "Well, you may be needing this in the future, but she certainly won't."

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: What happened with -- was she led into the bus after that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: She was on the bus by the time he gave me the money. She remained on the bus throughout, but then I asked this young man, "Young man, can you tell me where these buses are headed for? There is no evacuation, this is not a convoy carrying the wounded."

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Did you have any kind of conversation with that soldier?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I'm telling you I asked him, "Young man, listen, can you tell me where these buses are going? This is no convoy, they are not in the process of evacuating the wounded, as far as I can see." And he replied, "Don't ask me, madam." And I said, "Well, why wouldn't I ask you? I am expecting that I should be evacuated." And he said, "Which particular bus do you want to know about? This one?" And I said, "Yes, this one. I want to know about this bus because my family is on that bus." And he said, "Well, madam, on this bus, all the people on this bus are Ustasha extremists, and they should be swallowed by the night in broad daylight."

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: What does that mean, "swallowed by the night"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Well, you know, that's what people say, that they will disappear in the course of that same day. Day or night made little difference to them at this point. It was certain that they would come to grief and that they would be killed. And then my husband started sobbing, telling me to take Tanja away and to take his necklace and his ring with me. And I said, "Sorry, Martin, but why do you want me to do that? And he said, "Take my child away. You see there is no single woman or a single child on this bus. It is only you and Tanja left now. Take her away."

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Did you see any other people that were boarded on that third bus than you have told us now? Or were in the bus already during those incidents happening?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: There weren't many people on that bus, about 50 [as interpreted]. I knew some of them. The young Kozul, Sinisa Glavasevic, Ivan, Tadija, Vulic, Ruzica, and another three persons I didn't know. The young Martin Jakubovski was brought there later on, once everyone else had already got on to the bus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. There is one thing in the transcript, page 51, line 13. The witness said there were 10 people and the transcript says 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mrs. Dosen, if you know the -- you said the young Kozul. Do you happen to know the first name of the young Kozul?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Josip. Josip Kozul. His body was also identified at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. What -- you mentioned here also when it comes to the jewels that he had on himself. What happened with those? I'm talking about your husband's jewels now.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: My husband had a hand-made necklace with a medallion containing an image of the Virgin Mary and there is Tanja's name engraved on the back. He told me to take the necklace and give it to Tanja because he always wanted her to have it. On his ring finger, he had a huge ring with the letters DM. He was always saying that his son would have that finger [as interpreted], but he had been wounded and his arm was swollen. He couldn't take the ring off. So I told him, "Listen, Martin, I'm not sending you to your grave, I'm not taking any jewellery off you now." However, he had managed somehow to get the necklace off himself and give it to Tanja. Tanja still has this necklace. That's the only thing that remains of her father.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: How did you feel about that, Mrs. Dosen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: It was a dreadful feeling. Even now, as I talk about these things, I can't help but wonder how I managed to survive all of this and how I managed to keep the presence of mind to be able to reason, to be able to know that I had to get Tanja out of there somehow. She was only 14 years of age. She was a child watching all this happening, watching her father crying, watching one of her uncles on that bus, watching the other uncle, watching her cousin there. She was sobbing too. It was a dreadful experience; it was pure chaos. But I told myself that I had to be the one to try.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, did you take any action? You mentioned here that there was a dreadful feeling, and you had your 14-year-old daughter, and his [sic] father was crying. Did you do any actions when you were standing there? And what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I turned to look at the other buses, and I spotted a tall officer with a black moustache wearing a camouflage uniform. I didn't know at this time who this person was. I just walked towards him, and I heard him being addressed as Major Sljivancanin. I stood right there in front of him and addressed him, "Excuse me, can I ask you a question?" He answered in a robust way, "Yes, go ahead. Ask me." And I said, "What are my daughter and I doing here since there seem to be no women and children around here?" And he said, "Have you been arrested?" My answer was, "Why on earth would I be arrested? Is this the convoy?" He just looked at me and said, "Well, yes. So why are you here?" And I said, "I am here because of my husband." And then he asked me, "Where is your husband?" And I said, "He is right there on the stretcher." And he said, "Why isn't he on the bus?" And I said, "Well, the stretcher is too big to be placed on the bus through that narrow door." And he said, "Well, they should put him on the bus. They should lift him on the bus." And I said, "Well, he's not able to even sit down." And he said, "Well, who is he?" And I said, "It's my husband." And he said, "Yes, I know that, but who specifically?" And I said, "Martin Dosen." And then he said, "Oh, it's Dosen." I gave him a strange look, wondering how on earth he knew who Martin Dosen was. And then I said, "Well, yes." And then he said, "Well, then, he should go." And then he was lost in thought for a moment, and then he raised two fingers to some two soldiers standing there in order to tell them to go back to the bus and bring Martin on the stretcher back. I thought at this point that they would take him back to the hospital, but they just left him lying in that corridor passage that I marked with the letter C. I asked Sljivancanin right away, "I have Martin's bag on me containing his personal belongings and clothes. What am I supposed to do with it?" And he said, "Well, the -- why would he need that?" And I said, "What do you think? Why would he need that?" And then he probably remembered what he had told me, what would he be needing that for, he probably won't be needing that any longer. And then he said, "Who do you think will carry these for him?" He looked at me ask said, "You know something, both you and your daughter, please go straight away to where the remaining women and children are," so I went straight back. I told Tanja to walk ahead of me. I stopped as I was passing Martin's stretcher. He was wearing a pullover and a plaster-cast on his arm. I covered him up to keep him warm but he just placed one hand across his eyes. And that was the last time we saw him alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. I would like you now to go back to the photograph and look at that again. You said, Mrs. Dosen, that you turned to the buses and that you spotted a tall officer and that you didn't know him by the time, but that he was addressed as Major Sljivancanin. Where were he standing when you spotted him in the scenery on the photograph? Can you please show us that on the photograph? If you remember it.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes. How would you like me to mark it with?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: We can mark it with the marking with an I.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And why did you address this specific officer?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: I noticed him issuing orders, giving out commands, and that everybody reported to him, addressed him. And one could clearly see that everyone came to him, be it the reservists or the soldiers. If anyone had any questions, they all turned to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, when you are saying "issuing orders," can you explain that a bit more, what you were observing in that sense?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: I noticed that the entire evacuation process was under his command, that the wounded are being distributed on to the buses, and when they were filled, additional military trucks came to pick up those wounded who couldn't move. And I can show it to you on the photograph. It was to my left. As I was returning toward the hospital, they were loading those who couldn't move. When I say "loading," they simply tossed them on to the trucks --

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: We're getting to that point --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: -- not thinking that these people were actually wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: But you said on my question, where you did turn to him. And you say that he was issuing orders and I wanted you to explain what you observed in doing so. And then I'm talking about before that moment, so to say, when you addressed him, not afterwards, what happened after you addressed him, but before that when you turned to him, and my question was, why you did so? And then you mentioned that he issued orders. Can you explain that, why you saying that, and what did he do in order for you to make that observation, that he was issuing orders before that moment when you were addressing him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: I believe he was the commander there. I also took into account his insignia, because I used to be married to an officer. I could recognise rank and I knew he was a major. Being a relatively high officer in the JNA, that means that one commands over a number of people. And it seemed only appropriate to address him directly. I tried to invoke some -- the human side inside him, but I tried to ask for some assistance, and I had nowhere else to turn to, knowing he was a JNA officer, and seeing him command.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. You mentioned here that you had no one else to turn to. Did you make any try before you addressed this tall officer in this respect in order to get some help?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I tried to speak to a friend of Martin by the name of Darko Vuk, aka Drki. I told him, "Why don't you help Martin, try to do something, at least return him to the hospital. You can see that things are not going well." He was wearing a camouflage uniform. He looked at me and he says, "Ah, you, the Dosens, there is a lot you need to account for."

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Did you say anything more, or that was it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: That was it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: You were talking about here, Mrs. Dosen, about this tall officer, and you also said that you didn't know his identity at time, but he was addressed as Major Sljivancanin. Can you expand that a little bit more, in what sense he was addressed as Mr. Sljivancanin, when you heard it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: In such a situation when one can't think straight, you grasp a straw, if there is one. I tried to do something, I moved to -- towards him, seeing he was a person with certain authority there, that he held a rank. There were no regular JNA soldiers there, only the reservists and the locals who joined them as well as the Chetniks. And I thought to myself, He was the only person to turn to, since he was commanding there, and if he should decide for me to go on that bus, so be it. Otherwise, I still need to try something.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. You mentioned also -- earlier that he was addressed as -- if I heard it right, as Major Sljivancanin. Did you hear that he was addressed to that specific name, Major Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: The soldiers around him were calling him Sir or Major, and they told me, "Yes, this is Major Sljivancanin."

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. You mentioned here that you were told to go to another direction and leaving your husband. Was that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And I would like you to look at another photograph now. And that is with the same exhibit, 170, and that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you wanting to tender the one --

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm sorry, to tender this into evidence, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The one that has been marked by the witness will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit number will be 172, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: So the next photograph is Exhibit 170, and the ERN number is 0053-1261. And I'm asking the witness if the witness has that photograph available in front of her. Yes, she has.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, you mentioned here earlier when you described what happened that military trucks arrived. Where were they coming from, and from what spot did you see that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Those military trucks had already been parked behind the hospital at the time. That is, on the very edge of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Which edge, Mrs. Dosen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: To my left.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Are you meaning this photograph or the other photograph that we were looking at? I know you had this photograph 1261 in front of you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: So do you mean that --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Pardon me. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: This photograph, Mrs. Dosen --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: One can't see that on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Can you see it on the other photograph, 1260, if you turn back to that? I'm sorry for the inconvenience.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: On this photograph, right here, on my left side.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: The witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness is pointing to a position at the left bottom of the photograph, Exhibit 172. That is the roadway, but as far to the left as the photograph shows it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Did you see those military trucks, how many there were, Mrs. Dosen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: There were three or four trucks. I'm certain that I saw two parked there, and there were some wounded who couldn't walk on the trucks already, and Martin was probably waiting his turn.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. Now when we have this photograph up again, can you please just show us without marking when -- where you saw your husband as -- the last time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Can you see this? Right here.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And can you please -- we'll continue this marking, mark where the military trucks were with the next letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: J.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And where Martin Dosen were left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: K.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Can you please do that, Mrs. Dosen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, and I would like to have that tendered into evidence as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's an exhibit already.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: So, Mrs. Dosen, back to the other photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems to me there was a misunderstanding when the witness was explaining. I failed to see the letter J on the photograph. She was supposed to, as suggested by Judge Parker, to mark the place where she saw her husband the last time and the trucks were supposed to be marked with K.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Negative. J was the trucks; K was where the witness saw her husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But we don't see the letter J.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's in the bushes. Camouflage, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. And now, Mrs. Dosen, move over to the next photograph that we did have before, number -- ERN number 1261 at the end. What happened next, Mrs. Dosen? You left your husband, and what did you and Tanja do?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Tanja and I returned to the other women and children awaiting the convoy and evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay. And where did you go? Can you show us that on the photograph here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: We went toward the main exit of the hospital, because the buses were located there. So we moved from here to the main exit, and that's where the convoy was formed. I wanted to add --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you see the position where the buses were on the photograph that's in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The buses for the women and children?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or the wounded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The women and children.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Here. Where the parked cars are. That's where the convoy was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, that's at the very bottom edge, lowest edge of the photograph. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's the main road going through the town. And that's the main gate to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that on the left lower corner of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, is there reason for those to be marked, Mrs. Tuma?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, on this photograph I wonder whether you would be good enough, Mrs. Dosen, to mark the main entrance of the hospital with a letter A.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One could barely see the main entrance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's almost off the photograph, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And could you mark with letter Bs roughly where you remember the buses for the women and children, letter B?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]. [Interpretation] It would be here. From the exit there were a number of buses, seven or eight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did they stretch away to the right, as you're looking at the photograph, along the roadway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would suggest there is not a great deal of point, Mrs. Tuma, in marking a number of Bs. We can get the impression. Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. Yes, Mrs. Tuma.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there something further with this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Not any more marking, but if it's easier for the witness, so to say, to remember what took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm conscious of the time. I think we might have a break now and then return to this photograph. What we will do, if you tender it, is receive it as an exhibit now and then the witness may use it to point out other things when she resumes her evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And received under the reference 173, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 25 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mrs. Tuma.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, did you ever see the buses you were talking about earlier, the four buses. Did you ever see them leave the area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We better make more clear which buses. The buses for the wounded or the buses for the women and children.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: The four buses that Mrs. Dosen marked before for the wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The wounded, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: The buses E1 to E4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you see them leave, Mrs. Dosen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I no longer saw the buses because I was returning toward the hospital, hence I could see them no longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, you mentioned also military trucks were arriving, and you also showed us on one of the photographs. Did you ever see them leaving the area?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did see the trucks. I could see them from the place where the women and children were. We saw the trucks with the wounded leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. And after you had left your husband you mentioned that you went to the other side of the hospital. And now we're on the photograph number ERN number 1261. So when you were in this area here, Mrs. Dosen, did you then see any representatives from the international organisations present?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: The representatives of the international community came around 11.00. They first entered the hospital to make a list of the wounded who remained in the hospital and they told us to go to the buses, because that was supposed to be the convoy to evacuate us, and they were together with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. You mentioned that the military trucks, you saw them leaving. And you also said here that the international organisations came around 11.00. Was there any difference in time between when you saw the military trucks leaving and when you saw the international organisations present at around 11.00?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes. The difference between in that the buses and trucks left after 8.00 a.m. and the representatives of the European Community came around 11.00, so at that time there were neither the buses nor the trucks behind the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: You're saying that the buses and trucks, they left after 8.00 a.m. Is it close to 8.00 or what do you mean by "after 8.00 a.m."?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes. The evacuation began around 7.00 a.m., and we must have waited for about an hour, hour and a half for the convoy to be formed. And when I was returned to join the other women and children, then the proper convoy was formed. The wounded were not put on the list by the European Community representatives. They are simply non-existent in those terms, and I would like to hear from Mr. Sljivancanin where he took them to.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, we are -- I only want you to answer my questions, please. Can you please continue what you were saying before that when it comes to the timing?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: There was an hour or an hour and a half between the moment when the trucks left or that is from the moment when I could no longer see them, and the moment that the European Community representatives came.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. And where did you end up finally on that day, you and your daughter?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Myself, my daughter, Martin's mother, two under-age children, Ljiljana, Tadija's wife, and her daughter Alma, we were all on the same bus that was supposed to be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And, Mrs. Dosen, where did you end up finally? What location?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: We were told that we will travel through Bogdanovci, being the only Croatian village that was still open to communication, and via Bogdanovci, we were supposed to reach Vinkovci. We boarded the buses, and we were told that we are to go to Vinkovci and that we are being expected there when we leave Vukovar, but things didn't go that way. We were taken through the centre of the town toward Velepromet. As we were being driven, the scene was horrific. There were people who tried to reach the hospital, because they had heard about the convoy and the evacuation, but they never managed to reach the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: I presume that the liberators --

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, you said you were taken to Velepromet. And directly after that, where did you then go to next location, if there were any location that you went to? Just the name, please.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And was that the end location for you and your daughter, or were you transported anywhere else after Sremska Mitrovica? And where to, then?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: From Sremska Mitrovica where we spent the night, we were told there that Croatia won't have us, and that they don't know what to do with us, that Zagreb cannot take us in, that they have too many already. And we were told that we can go anywhere, provided it is a locality in Croatia and not in Serbia. The international community representatives tried to negotiate with them, and they managed to secure the route via Bijeljina to reach Djakovo. Therefore, we travelled for two days and a night to reach -- 60 kilometres to reach Djakovo. Instead we had to go all the way through Bosnia to reach Djakovo. And then Tanja and I stayed in Djakovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And Mrs. Dosen, was that your final destination?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: No. After Djakovo I went to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. Just a matter of clarification. I would like you now to lead you back to the hospital. What happened there, just -- concerning just one issue, and one clarification, please. That -- did you ever, during the last two days on the 19th and the 20th November, 1991, did you have any direct dealings with Dr. Bosanac yourself?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. And after that I will go through some exhibits. And that is concerning 65 ter exhibit number 243, starting with the first page, with its ERN number 02189326. Thank you. Mrs. Dosen, you told us earlier that there were a medical record that you kept in your possession. Can you recognise this page?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And for the Court, there is also an English translation, bearing the number -- ERN number 00582903.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, can you please tell the Court what this page says that you have in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: This page is my husband's case history, as well as the time and date that he was admitted to the Vukovar Medical Centre. This was attached to his bed. It's a document that I brought back from the Vukovar Hospital and the original is in my possession.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Can you please tell us where the date on this -- on this document that Martin Dosen was admitted to the hospital, what date does that show on this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, it's square number eight. It says date admitted, on the 16th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And then we can move on to the next page, page number 2, bearing the ERN number 02189327. And also the English version, it's 00582904.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And Mrs. Dosen, this page that you have in front of you here now, is that part of your medical record that you had in your possession from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And do you know what -- what is said on that page?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Well, as much as I can read, that he was admitted to the hospital, that he had fallen from the third floor, fallen down from the third floor, that his spine was to be X-rayed, and the rest appears to be in Latin.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: When the rest is in Latin, did you take any actions in order to have that explained to you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I asked Dr. Njavro and he explained it to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Was there --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: He was the one who admitted Martin to the hospital the first time around, when he was wounded for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. Were there any other doctor that did explain this page for you, what it contained?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: What's his name, he is an orthopaedist. Aleksijevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: That explanation, did you get that -- in what kind of form did you get that explanation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Martin was listed as missing, and I wanted to exercise whatever rights I had as the wife of a missing Croat defender. I needed to apply in order to get the documents to certify that Martin had been wounded, and then I needed a doctor's translation of the exact diagnosis, and then Dr. Aleksijevic obliged. He wrote up the finding and the explanation attached to Martin's case history and wounding.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. So now I would like to you see on another document, to see if that is that explanation that you are talking about right now. And the ERN number for the B/C/S version, so to say, is 02189333. And the English translation is bearing the number 00582907.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And we are --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: That's the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay. And also we are waiting to have -- is it -- do we have it here on the screen as well? Okay. Is this that document, Mrs. Dosen, that was -- you were talking about giving you an explanation what was said in -- on page number 2 of the medical record?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And I would like for the Court also to tender the English translation into evidence. And also the B/C/S version of course. And I will go through the rest of the medical record, but I don't need to read it out while I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you want to tender the whole of the medical report?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be received under reference 174, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And now the translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Translation as well, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's been recorded under the same document, so it's already become an exhibit as part of 174.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, now we turn to another page here that is part of the medical record as far as I can see it. And that is bearing the ERN number 02189330. So that is the B/C/S version, yes, that's it. And then I will, for the Court, mention the English version that is 00582905. Have you seen this document before, Mrs. Dosen? This page?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: And when did you --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: I have the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please explain what we can see on that page as far as concerning your knowledge of it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: This is a temperature chart charting the patient's temperature on a daily basis. So if you look at the chart, you can see the dates right there, the 16th of November, which is the day that Martin was admitted to the hospital, the 17th, the 18th, the 19th, and the 20th is the last date that we have any data in relation to. Which means that that was the day he left the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Can you read out from this document what date the temperature was taken on Martin Dosen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: It says here under number one, the 16th of November, number two, the 17th of November, number three, the 18th of November. We have no entries in relation to the 19th or the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Dosen.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Finally I would like to deal with one last document that you mentioned briefly before. And that is bearing the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you want to tender the --

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Yes, the whole medical record, that is part of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is already part, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: The next and the last document is bearing the B/C/S, so to say, ERN number 02189332. English version is 00582906. I would like to tender that as well into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that part of Exhibit 174?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Yes. My understanding, it's part of that. Right? Yeah. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Mrs. Dosen, can you please explain as to what this document says?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA DOSEN
utterances.text: This certifies that the first time Martin was wounded was in August when he was wounded in his leg by a shell. He received outpatient treatment by Dr. Juraj Njavro. As I said earlier, I had to gather all these documents, because Martin was no longer alive, and I had certain entitlements as the wife of a fallen Croatian defender, but I had to have everything black and white, in writing. And I believed both Dr. Njavro and Dr. Aleksijevic will be glad to confirm this for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mrs. Dosen. I'm done with my examination-in-chief, Your Honour. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mrs. Tuma. You have the option, Mr. Vasic. We can break now, or you can have six minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I could go on for six minutes, but that is certainly no more than three questions. If that's what it takes, I'm ready. But perhaps the witness might prefer to start afresh tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I think we will call it a day then, Mr. Vasic, and you can be ready for a speedy cross-examination tomorrow. Mrs. Dosen, we will adjourn now for the day, and we will resume tomorrow again at 2.15. The court officer who is with you will give you detailed instructions about tomorrow. But we will now adjourn and we will continue tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
